results.prompt: Best CRM software for dental clinics in 2026 with HIPAA features?
results.stdout:
For most dental clinics in 2026, **RevenueWell is the best overall CRM-style platform**. It is dental-specific, integrates with common practice-management systems, and combines recall/reactivation, campaigns, scheduling, messaging, forms, reviews, payments, and a patient portal.

“CRM” in dentistry usually means a patient-engagement layer connected to the practice-management system—not a conventional sales CRM.

| Recommendation | Best for | Notable HIPAA/security capabilities |
|---|---|---|
| **[RevenueWell](https://www.revenuewell.com/)** | Best overall for independent dental practices | HIPAA-compliant messaging and forms, secure portal/file sharing, encrypted PMS data transfer; vendor identifies itself as a business associate. See its [HIPAA statement](https://www.revenuewell.com/hipaa-compliance). |
| **[NexHealth](https://www.nexhealth.com/)** | Best patient experience and front-office automation | Online booking, automated forms, recalls, messaging, payments and insurance verification; broad dental PMS integration. NexHealth reports [HIPAA and SOC 2 compliance](https://help.nexhealth.com/en/articles/12754290-what-is-nexhealth-s-legal-and-security-compliance-status). |
| **[Weave](https://www.getweave.com/industry/dentistry/)** | Best communications and phones | Integrated VoIP, texting, call pop, missed-call text, reviews and payments. Published safeguards include encrypted transmission, authentication, role-based access, secure storage and message/VoIP logs; see its [dental HIPAA guide](https://www.getweave.com/hipaa-for-dental-offices-full-guide-for-dentists). |
| **[CareStack](https://carestack.com/)** | Best all-in-one CRM plus practice management | Suitable when replacing the PMS—not merely adding CRM. Includes scheduling, clinical, billing, patient engagement and analytics. Security features include audit trails, job-based permissions, encrypted communication, backups and recovery; see [CareStack’s HIPAA page](https://carestack.com/dental-software/features/hipaa-compliant). |
| **[Solutionreach](https://www.solutionreach.com/)** | Best for established groups and multi-location engagement | Centralized messaging, reminders, intake, scheduling, surveys and payments, with HIPAA-compliant automated communications and configurable user permissions. |
| **[Salesforce Health Cloud](https://www.salesforce.com/healthcare/health-cloud/)** | Best for large DSOs with complex referral and growth operations | Powerful enterprise CRM, workflow and analytics, but requires implementation and dental/PMS integrations. Salesforce offers a BAA only for covered services; confirm scope through its [HIPAA compliance portal](https://compliance.salesforce.com/en/categories/hipaa). |

My practical shortlist:

- **Solo or small group:** RevenueWell
- **Modern booking and automated front desk:** NexHealth
- **Phone-heavy office:** Weave
- **Replacing several systems with one platform:** CareStack
- **Large DSO with an IT/CRM team:** Salesforce Health Cloud
- **Multi-location patient outreach without a full Salesforce build:** Solutionreach

Before signing, require the vendor to provide:

## Creamy Mushroom & Spinach Pasta

Ready in about 25 minutes; serves 4.

**Ingredients**

- 12 oz (340 g) pasta
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 8 oz (225 g) mushrooms, sliced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 5 oz (140 g) fresh spinach
- ¾ cup heavy cream or half-and-half
- ½ cup grated Parmesan
- Salt and black pepper
- Optional: red-pepper flakes, lemon juice, or chopped parsley

**Method**

1. Boil the pasta in well-salted water until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
2. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and leave them mostly undisturbed for 3–4 minutes so they brown; stir and cook another 2–3 minutes.
3. Add garlic and a pinch of pepper flakes. Cook for 30 seconds.
4. Lower the heat. Stir in the cream, Parmesan, and about ½ cup pasta water.
5. Add the spinach and cook until wilted. Toss in the pasta, adding more pasta water as needed for a silky sauce.
6. Season with salt and pepper. Finish with a squeeze of lemon and extra Parmesan.

For extra protein, add white beans, rotisserie chicken, or Italian sausage. For a lighter version, skip the cream and emulsify Parmesan with ¾–1 cup of pasta water.
